subject: physics
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT an energy store?
questions.explain: Electrical is a transfer pathway that moves energy between stores, not an energy store itself.

questions.q: What is the equation for the kinetic energy of a moving object?
questions.explain: Kinetic energy equals one half of mass multiplied by speed squared.

questions.q: Which equation gives the gravitational potential energy gained when an object is raised?
questions.explain: Gravitational potential energy equals mass multiplied by gravitational field strength multiplied by height.

questions.q: For a spring within the limit of proportionality, the elastic potential energy stored is given by:
questions.explain: Elastic potential energy equals one half of the spring constant multiplied by the extension squared.

questions.q: How is the efficiency of an energy transfer defined?
options: Useful output energy transfer ÷ total input energy transfer
Total input energy transfer ÷ useful output energy transfer
Useful output energy transfer × total input energy transfer
questions.explain: Efficiency is the useful output energy transfer divided by the total input energy transfer.

questions.q: Which equation relates the energy needed to change the temperature of a substance to its specific heat capacity?
questions.explain: The energy transferred equals mass multiplied by specific heat capacity multiplied by the temperature change.

questions.q: Which of these is a renewable energy resource?
questions.explain: Wind is renewable because it is continually replenished and will not run out.

questions.q: Which set lists only fossil fuels?
questions.explain: The three fossil fuels are coal, oil (petroleum) and natural gas.

questions.q: Which statement best expresses the principle of conservation of energy?
options: Energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transferred, stored or dissipated
Energy is always completely converted into useful forms
Energy can be created when a system does work
Energy is destroyed whenever friction acts
questions.explain: Energy is never created or destroyed; it is only transferred between stores, stored or dissipated.

questions.q: When energy is 'dissipated' during a transfer, this means it is:
options: Transferred to the surroundings, usually by heating, in less useful ways
Destroyed and permanently lost from the universe
Stored in the chemical store of the object
questions.explain: Dissipated energy is spread out to the surroundings, typically warming them, and becomes less useful.

questions.q: Lubricating the moving parts of a machine reduces unwanted energy transfers mainly by:
options: Increasing the mass of the parts
Raising the temperature of the machine
Increasing the thermal conductivity of the parts
questions.explain: Lubrication lowers friction, so less energy is dissipated by heating as the parts move.

questions.q: To reduce unwanted energy loss from a house, cavity walls are filled with insulation. This works best if the insulating material has:
questions.explain: A low thermal conductivity means energy is transferred through the walls more slowly, reducing losses.

questions.q: Describing an energy resource as 'renewable' means that it:
options: Is being (or can be) replenished as it is used and will not run out
Produces no waste products at all
Can always meet demand at any time
Is always cheaper than non-renewable resources
questions.explain: A renewable resource is replenished as fast as it is used, so it does not run out.

questions.q: Why are fossil fuels often described as more reliable than wind or solar power?
options: They can supply energy whenever it is needed, regardless of weather or time of day
questions.explain: Fossil fuel power stations can be run on demand, whereas wind and solar depend on variable weather and daylight.

questions.q: In a closed system, the net change in the total energy is:
questions.explain: A closed system exchanges no energy with its surroundings, so its total energy stays the same.

questions.q: A major environmental disadvantage of burning fossil fuels is that it:
options: Releases carbon dioxide, contributing to global warming
Uses up the world's supply of wind
Reduces the reliability of the supply
questions.explain: Burning fossil fuels releases carbon dioxide, a greenhouse gas linked to global warming and climate change.

questions.q: A ball of mass 2 kg moves at a speed of 3 m/s. What is its kinetic energy?
A 5 kg mass is lifted 10 m. Using g = 9.8 N/kg, how much gravitational potential energy does it gain?
A device is supplied with 120 J of energy and transfers 30 J usefully. What is its efficiency?
questions.explain: Efficiency = useful output ÷ total input = 30 ÷ 120 = 0.25 = 25%.

questions.q: A motor transfers 600 J of energy in 4 s. What is its power?
questions.explain: Power = energy transferred ÷ time = 600 ÷ 4 = 150 W.
